newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips firm, tech stocks sluggish.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips firm, tech stocks sluggish.

text.p: The Dow industrials were slightly firmer on Monday, underpinned by a strong bond market and dollar but wary ahead of this week's economic data.
But technology stocks were weaker, as shares of personal computer makers and market heavyweights like Intel Corp and Microsoft Corp dipped.
The Dow Jones Industrial average was up 16 points at 8130 while the long bond gained 8/32 to 6.44 percent.
"We've got a good fixed income market, and we keep being impressed by how well earnings are coming in," said Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics.
"There is no bad news and the dollar is strong, which never hurts," he said.
Both bond and stock markets anxiously awaited the release of the second quarter employment cost index on Tuesday and the July employment report on Friday, as well as other data.
The Nasdaq composite declined around five points to 1565.
Intel, which announced plans to acquire computer graphics supplier Chips and Technologies Inc for $397 million, dipped 11/16 to 88-1/2.
The chipmaker was expected to have slashed prices on the Pentium microprocessor by up to 50 percent on Sunday.
